outputs.L1: A process and plant for the continuous conversion of a hydrocarbonaceous feed gas into a synthesis gas comprising carbon monoxide and hydrogen, wherein the H₂/CO molar ratio of the product gases can be varied over a wide range. This is achieved by admixing at least a portion of a methane-rich gas obtained during fractionation of the raw synthesis gas with the feed gas mixture. Alternatively, to lower the H₂/CO ratio, at least a portion of the H₂ product gas and/or an increased fraction, relative to normal process operation, of a hydrogen-rich gas is admixed with the heating gas mixture. To increase the H₂/CO ratio, at least a portion of the CO product gas and/or an increased fraction, relative to normal process operation, of a carbon monoxide-rich gas is admixed with the heating gas mixture.
outputs.L2: A method and facility continuously transform a hydrocarbon-containing feed gas into synthesis gas containing hydrogen and carbon monoxide, while allowing the product’s H₂/CO molar ratio to be adjusted over a broad range. At least some of the methane-rich stream produced during raw synthesis-gas fractionation is recycled into the feed-gas mixture. To reduce the H₂/CO ratio, the heating-gas mixture alternatively receives at least part of the hydrogen product stream and/or a larger-than-normal portion of a hydrogen-rich stream. To raise the H₂/CO ratio, at least part of the carbon monoxide product stream and/or an increased portion of a carbon monoxide-rich stream, relative to standard process operation, is instead added to the heating-gas mixture.
outputs.L3:
The process continuously converts a hydrocarbon-containing feed gas into a synthesis gas comprising primarily carbon monoxide and hydrogen. The operating conditions can be controlled so that the molar hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide ratio (H₂/CO) of the resulting product gas is adjustable over a broad range.

During fractionation of the raw synthesis gas, a methane-rich gas stream is recovered. At least part of this stream is recycled and combined with the hydrocarbonaceous feed gas, thereby returning unconverted or recovered methane to the conversion process.

The H₂/CO ratio is regulated by modifying the composition of the heating-gas mixture. When a lower H₂/CO ratio is required, hydrogen product gas—or an increased proportion of a hydrogen-rich gas fraction—is added to the heating-gas mixture. Conversely, when a higher H₂/CO ratio is desired, carbon monoxide product gas—or an increased proportion of a carbon monoxide-rich gas fraction—is introduced into the heating-gas mixture. This coordinated recycling and heating-gas adjustment enables continuous production of synthesis gas with a composition tailored to downstream requirements.
outputs.L4:
A continuous process and corresponding plant are provided for converting a hydrocarbonaceous feed gas into a synthesis gas containing carbon monoxide and hydrogen. The process is designed to permit flexible control of the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio (H₂/CO ratio) in the final synthesis-gas product, allowing the same plant to supply gas compositions suitable for a variety of downstream applications.

The hydrocarbonaceous feed gas, which may contain methane and other light hydrocarbons, is introduced into a synthesis-gas generation section. There, it is converted into a raw synthesis gas by reforming, partial oxidation, or a combination of these reactions. Heat required for the conversion is supplied at least partly by combusting a heating mixture in an associated heating or combustion section.

After cooling and, where appropriate, removal of water, carbon dioxide, or other impurities, at least part of the raw synthesis gas is sent to a fractionation or separation section. This section produces one or more gas fractions having different compositions. In particular, it may generate a methane-rich fraction, a hydrogen-rich fraction, and a carbon monoxide-rich fraction.

At least part of the methane-rich fractionation gas is recycled to the synthesis-gas generation section. Recycling this methane-containing stream increases utilization of the hydrocarbon feed and reduces the amount of unconverted methane discharged with the product. The recycled gas may be combined with the fresh feed gas before conversion or introduced separately into the conversion section.

The H₂/CO ratio of the synthesis-gas product is adjusted by selectively routing hydrogen-rich or carbon monoxide-rich gas to the heating mixture. When hydrogen-rich gas is diverted from the product stream and added to the heating mixture, hydrogen is preferentially removed from the synthesis-gas product, thereby lowering its H₂/CO ratio. Conversely, when carbon monoxide-rich gas is diverted to the heating mixture, carbon monoxide is preferentially removed from the product, causing the H₂/CO ratio to increase.

The quantities of hydrogen-rich gas and carbon monoxide-rich gas supplied to the heating mixture can be controlled continuously in response to a measured or desired product-gas composition. Flow-control valves, composition analyzers, and a process-control system may regulate the respective streams while maintaining the required heat input to the synthesis-gas generation section. The heating mixture may also include methane-rich gas, purge gas, fresh fuel, or other combustible process streams as necessary to maintain stable combustion and satisfy the plant’s thermal requirements.

By coordinating methane-rich gas recycle with selective use of hydrogen-rich and carbon monoxide-rich fractions as heating fuel, the process provides broad and continuous adjustment of the product H₂/CO ratio without requiring major changes to the principal conversion equipment. The plant can therefore produce synthesis gas tailored for different uses, including methanol synthesis, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, hydrogen production, reducing-gas applications, and other chemical processes requiring a specified hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide ratio.
outputs.L5:
**This**

“This” is a small but powerful word. It directs attention to what is close, present, or important: this moment, this place, this idea. It can create clarity by identifying exactly what we mean, but its meaning always depends on context.

In everyday speech, “this” connects people to immediate experiences. We say, “Look at this,” when we want to share something interesting, or “This matters,” when we wish to emphasize significance. Although simple, the word reminds us to focus on what is here and now—this opportunity, this challenge, and this moment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a process and plant that continuously converts hydrocarbonaceous feed gas into synthesis gas with an adjustable H2/CO molar ratio.
counterfactuals.output: A process and plant are disclosed for continuously converting a hydrocarbonaceous feed gas into synthesis gas having an adjustable H₂/CO molar ratio. The feed gas is mixed with steam, an oxygen-containing gas, carbon dioxide, or combinations thereof and supplied to a reforming section comprising at least one catalytic reformer, partial-oxidation reactor, or autothermal reformer. A raw synthesis gas containing hydrogen, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, steam, and residual hydrocarbons is produced. At least a portion of the raw synthesis gas is selectively passed through a water-gas-shift unit, while a remaining portion bypasses the unit. The shifted and bypassed streams are combined to form a product synthesis gas. A control system adjusts one or more of the steam-to-carbon ratio, oxygen-to-carbon ratio, carbon dioxide addition rate, and shifted-to-bypassed stream ratio in response to a measured product composition, thereby maintaining a selected H₂/CO molar ratio during continuous operation. Heat recovery and recycle circuits improve thermal efficiency and carbon utilization.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for controlling the hydrogen-to-carbon-monoxide ratio in syngas by recycling methane-rich fractionation gas to the feed and selectively adding hydrogen-rich or carbon-monoxide-rich streams to the heating gas.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention provides a method and system for controlling the hydrogen-to-carbon-monoxide ratio of synthesis gas produced from a methane-containing feed. The raw syngas is fractionated into a methane-rich stream, a hydrogen-rich stream, a carbon-monoxide-rich stream, and a product syngas stream. At least part of the methane-rich fractionation gas is recycled to the reforming or conversion feed, increasing methane utilization and stabilizing syngas production.

An analyzer measures the hydrogen-to-carbon-monoxide ratio in the product syngas, and a controller selectively routes one or more separated streams to the heating-gas system. When the product contains excess hydrogen, a hydrogen-rich stream is diverted to the heating gas, thereby lowering the product H₂/CO ratio. When the product contains excess carbon monoxide, a carbon-monoxide-rich stream is diverted to the heating gas, thereby increasing the product H₂/CO ratio. The diverted streams are combusted to supply process heat, reducing the need for external fuel.

Coordinated control of methane-rich recycle and the selective use of hydrogen-rich or carbon-monoxide-rich fractions as heating gas allows the process to maintain a desired syngas composition despite changes in feed composition, operating conditions, or downstream demand.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of a syngas production method in which the H2/CO ratio can be lowered by routing hydrogen product gas to the heating mixture or increased by routing CO product gas to it.
counterfactuals.output: Syngas is produced by converting a hydrocarbon feed with steam and/or oxygen in a heated reforming zone. The resulting gas is separated into hydrogen- and carbon-monoxide-rich product streams. A controlled portion of either stream is recycled to the heating mixture and combusted to supply process heat: recycling hydrogen selectively lowers the net product H₂/CO ratio, while recycling carbon monoxide selectively increases it. Flow control of the recycle streams enables continuous adjustment of syngas composition while recovering their heating value.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate patent-style language for a continuous hydrocarbon gas conversion system that uses internal recycle streams from raw synthesis-gas fractionation to vary the product H2/CO ratio over a wide range.
counterfactuals.output:
## Title

**Continuous Hydrocarbon Gas Conversion with Internal Recycle Control of Product Hydrogen-to-Carbon Monoxide Ratio**

## Abstract

A continuous system and method are provided for converting a hydrocarbon-containing feed into a synthesis-gas product having an adjustable hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio. A raw synthesis-gas stream produced in a hydrocarbon conversion reactor is fractionated into at least a hydrogen-enriched fraction and a carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction. At least a portion of one or more fractions is returned as an internal recycle stream to the reactor, a feed-conditioning zone, or a fractionation zone. Relative recycle rates are varied while maintaining continuous operation to control the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio of the exported synthesis-gas product over a selected operating range. The system may additionally recover and recycle carbon dioxide, unconverted hydrocarbon, steam, or combinations thereof. A controller can manipulate recycle flow, purge flow, fractionation conditions, reactant addition, and product withdrawal in response to a measured or calculated product composition.

## Technical Field

The disclosure relates to continuous conversion of hydrocarbon gases to synthesis gas and, more particularly, to control of a product hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide ratio by selective internal recycling of fractions obtained from raw synthesis-gas fractionation.

## Summary of the Disclosure

In one aspect, a hydrocarbon-containing feed is continuously introduced into a conversion zone and contacted with steam, an oxygen-containing gas, carbon dioxide, or a combination thereof to produce a raw synthesis-gas stream comprising hydrogen and carbon monoxide. The raw synthesis-gas stream is subjected to one or more fractionation operations to form compositionally distinct fractions, including a hydrogen-enriched fraction and a carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction.

A first portion of at least one fraction is withdrawn as product or incorporated into a product blend, while a second portion is recycled within the system. By varying the relative amounts and destinations of the recycled fractions, the net production, conversion, and export rates of hydrogen and carbon monoxide can be independently influenced. The product hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio may thereby be changed without shutting down the conversion zone and, in certain embodiments, without materially changing the hydrocarbon-feed throughput.

The fractionation operation may comprise cryogenic separation, partial condensation, distillation, pressure-swing adsorption, temperature-swing adsorption, membrane separation, solvent absorption, or any combination thereof. The conversion zone may comprise a steam reformer, partial-oxidation reactor, autothermal reformer, catalytic partial-oxidation reactor, dry-reforming reactor, plasma reactor, electrically heated reformer, or a combination of two or more such reactors.

Suitable internal recycle streams include:

1. a hydrogen-enriched recycle stream;
2. a carbon-monoxide-enriched recycle stream;
3. a carbon-dioxide-enriched recycle stream;
4. an unconverted-hydrocarbon-enriched recycle stream;
5. a condensate or steam recycle stream; and
6. mixtures thereof.

A hydrogen-enriched fraction may be recycled to the conversion zone, used as fuel, exported, or blended with another fraction. A carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction may be recycled upstream of or into the conversion zone, blended into the synthesis-gas product, or directed to a carbon-monoxide conversion zone. A carbon-dioxide-enriched fraction may be recycled to promote dry reforming or otherwise decrease the product hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide ratio. Conversely, steam addition, hydrogen-enriched fraction blending, or carbon-monoxide conversion may be increased to raise the product ratio.

A control system may receive a signal representative of the hydrogen concentration, carbon monoxide concentration, hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide ratio, flow rate, pressure, temperature, or downstream demand of the product stream. The control system adjusts one or more recycle valves, compressors, fractionator operating parameters, reactant flow rates, purge rates, or product blending rates to maintain a selected ratio.

## Exemplary Claims

1. **A continuous hydrocarbon conversion system comprising:**

   a hydrocarbon conversion zone configured to continuously receive a hydrocarbon-containing feed and at least one reactant selected from steam, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and combinations thereof, and to produce a raw synthesis-gas stream comprising hydrogen and carbon monoxide;

   a fractionation assembly fluidly coupled to the hydrocarbon conversion zone and configured to separate at least a portion of the raw synthesis-gas stream into a hydrogen-enriched fraction and a carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction;

   a product manifold configured to receive at least a portion of one or both of the hydrogen-enriched fraction and the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction and to discharge a synthesis-gas product;

   a first recycle conduit configured to return at least a portion of the hydrogen-enriched fraction, the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction, or both, to a location upstream of the product manifold; and

   a control system configured to vary a flow rate through the first recycle conduit relative to a flow rate supplied to the product manifold, thereby varying a hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio of the synthesis-gas product during continuous operation of the hydrocarbon conversion zone.

2. The system of claim 1, wherein the first recycle conduit is configured to return at least a portion of the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction to the hydrocarbon conversion zone.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein the first recycle conduit is configured to return at least a portion of the hydrogen-enriched fraction to the hydrocarbon conversion zone, a feed-conditioning zone, or the fractionation assembly.

4. The system of claim 1, further comprising a carbon-dioxide separation stage configured to produce a carbon-dioxide-enriched fraction and a second recycle conduit configured to return at least a portion of the carbon-dioxide-enriched fraction to the hydrocarbon conversion zone.

5. The system of claim 4, wherein the control system is configured to increase recycling of the carbon-dioxide-enriched fraction to decrease the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio of the synthesis-gas product.

6. The system of claim 1, wherein the fractionation assembly comprises at least one of a cryogenic separator, a partial condenser, a distillation column, a membrane module, a pressure-swing adsorption unit, a temperature-swing adsorption unit, and a solvent absorption unit.

7. The system of claim 1, wherein the hydrocarbon conversion zone comprises at least one of a steam-methane reformer, an autothermal reformer, a partial-oxidation reactor, a catalytic partial-oxidation reactor, and a dry-reforming reactor.

8. The system of claim 1, further comprising a water-gas-shift reactor selectively operable to receive at least one of the raw synthesis-gas stream, the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction, and a recycle stream.

9. The system of claim 1, wherein the fractionation assembly is further configured to produce an unconverted-hydrocarbon-enriched fraction, and wherein at least a portion of the unconverted-hydrocarbon-enriched fraction is recycled to the hydrocarbon conversion zone.

10. The system of claim 1, wherein the control system is configured to vary the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio while maintaining the hydrocarbon-containing feed within ±20 percent of a selected feed rate.

11. The system of claim 1, further comprising a composition analyzer configured to generate a signal representative of the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio of the synthesis-gas product, wherein the control system is configured to adjust the first recycle conduit in response to the signal.

12. The system of claim 1, wherein the control system is configured to establish different product-ratio setpoints without discontinuing flow of the hydrocarbon-containing feed.

13. **A method for continuously producing synthesis gas having an adjustable composition, the method comprising:**

   continuously converting a hydrocarbon-containing feed in a conversion zone to form a raw synthesis-gas stream comprising hydrogen and carbon monoxide;

   fractionating at least a portion of the raw synthesis-gas stream to form a hydrogen-enriched fraction and a carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction;

   forming a synthesis-gas product from selected amounts of the hydrogen-enriched fraction, the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction, or both;

   recycling at least a portion of at least one fraction derived from the raw synthesis-gas stream to the conversion zone, a feed-conditioning zone, or a fractionation zone; and

   changing a recycle rate of the at least one fraction relative to a product withdrawal rate to change a hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio of the synthesis-gas product while continuously converting the hydrocarbon-containing feed.

14. The method of claim 13, comprising decreasing the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio by increasing at least one of carbon dioxide recycle, carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction recycle, carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction blending, and dry-reforming activity.

15. The method of claim 13, comprising increasing the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio by increasing at least one of steam addition, hydrogen-enriched fraction blending, hydrogen recovery, and water-gas-shift conversion.

16. The method of claim 13, wherein changing the recycle rate changes the hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio between a first setpoint and a second setpoint differing from the first setpoint by at least 0.5.

17. The method of claim 13, wherein the synthesis-gas product is controlled to have a hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio selectable within a range of about 0.2:1 to about 10:1.

18. The method of claim 13, further comprising measuring the composition of the synthesis-gas product and automatically adjusting at least one of a recycle flow, a purge flow, a steam flow, an oxygen flow, a carbon dioxide flow, and a fractionation operating condition in response to the measured composition.

19. The method of claim 13, wherein fractionating comprises removing water and carbon dioxide from the raw synthesis-gas stream before separating the hydrogen-enriched fraction from the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction.

20. The method of claim 13, wherein at least a portion of the hydrogen-enriched fraction or the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction is accumulated in an intermediate surge vessel to decouple fractionation flow from product demand.

21. **A control method for a continuous synthesis-gas plant, comprising:**

   receiving a target hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratio for an exported synthesis-gas stream;

   receiving a measured or inferred composition of the exported synthesis-gas stream;

   determining a deviation between the target ratio and an actual ratio;

   in response to the deviation, manipulating respective flow rates of at least two internal streams obtained by fractionation of raw synthesis gas, the at least two internal streams having different hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide molar ratios; and

   maintaining continuous production of raw synthesis gas while causing the actual ratio to approach the target ratio.

22. The control method of claim 21, wherein manipulating the respective flow rates comprises changing a split between recycle and export for at least one of a hydrogen-enriched fraction and a carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction.

23. The control method of claim 21, further comprising imposing one or more constraints selected from a reactor temperature constraint, compressor capacity constraint, carbon deposition constraint, fractionator capacity constraint, product pressure constraint, and minimum purge constraint.

## Exemplary Operational Description

During a first operating mode, a relatively greater portion of a hydrogen-enriched fraction may be blended into the product, while a carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction or carbon-dioxide-enriched fraction is recycled. This mode provides a comparatively high product hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide ratio.

During a second operating mode, a greater portion of the carbon-monoxide-enriched fraction may be blended into the product, hydrogen may be selectively withdrawn or recycled, and carbon dioxide may be introduced into the conversion zone. This mode provides a comparatively low product hydrogen-to-carbon monoxide ratio.

Transitions between the operating modes may be performed progressively by ramping recycle and blending valves according to predetermined limits. Surge vessels, variable-speed recycle compressors, bypass conduits, and feed-forward control based on downstream product demand may be used to reduce pressure or composition disturbances. A purge stream may be maintained to limit accumulation of nitrogen, argon, methane, or other nonreactive or weakly reactive constituents.

As used herein, “internal recycle” includes a stream derived directly or indirectly from the raw synthesis-gas stream and returned to any upstream location within the same integrated conversion system, whether or not the stream undergoes compression, heating, cooling, reaction, adsorption, condensation, or other intermediate treatment. “Hydrogen-enriched” and “carbon-monoxide-enriched” denote enrichment relative to the stream supplied to the applicable separation operation and do not require production of substantially pure hydrogen or carbon monoxide.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, in one paragraph, a process and associated plant for adjustable-ratio synthesis gas production, including methane-rich gas recycle and alternative enrichment of the heating gas with either hydrogen-rich or carbon-monoxide-rich fractions.
counterfactuals.output: An adjustable-ratio synthesis-gas process feeds a methane-containing gas, optionally with steam and/or carbon dioxide, to a heated reformer that produces crude synthesis gas containing hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and residual methane; the crude gas is cooled and separated into a hydrogen-rich fraction, a carbon-monoxide-rich fraction, and a methane-rich fraction, with the methane-rich fraction recycled to the reformer feed to increase conversion and reduce losses. The desired H₂/CO product ratio is set by controlling the amounts of the hydrogen-rich and carbon-monoxide-rich fractions blended into the synthesis-gas product, while surplus fraction is used to enrich the reformer heating gas: hydrogen-rich gas may be added when clean, high-reactivity fuel is preferred, or carbon-monoxide-rich gas may be added when hydrogen is to be conserved and excess CO is available. The associated plant includes the reformer and burner or furnace, feed-mixing and compression equipment, heat-recovery and cooling units, gas-separation equipment, methane-recycle piping and compressor, separate H₂-rich and CO-rich lines with control valves, a product-blending system, and selectable connections from either enriched fraction to the heating-gas supply.
